clue.text: (& 8dn.) Eventual expulsion of binge drinker with disgusting, far-reaching effects?

definitions.text: Eventual expulsion of binge drinker with disgusting, far-reaching effects?

parts.note: surface reading: a heavy drinker finally being thrown out of the pub
setter's reading: what the drinker's stomach finally expels, travelling a long way

explanation.surface: A boozer is finally ejected from a bar, with grim consequences for everyone around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expulsion' suggests being thrown out of the pub; it is what comes up, forcefully and far, at the end of a binge.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent sickness that sends stomach contents shooting a long distance is the classic end of a heavy drinking session.

clue.text: Flesh and blood male dominated by Brenda

definitions.note: a noun phrase in sense: the territory Brenda rules

parts.note: flesh and blood means actual, not imaginary
standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A flesh-and-blood man is bossed about by a woman called Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, so what she dominates is her kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is the territory ruled by a monarch, and Private Eye's Brenda was the Queen.

clue.text: Male athlete's trick for keeping his equipment safely in place

definitions.text: for keeping his equipment safely in place
definitions.note: describes the thing by its purpose rather than naming it

parts.note: a jock is a male athlete, with the possessive s
a trap is a trick or snare

explanation.surface: A sportsman's dodge for stopping his genitals from bouncing around.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the athlete stays in the answer as the S joining the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: This supportive undergarment holds a sportsman's genitals firmly while he runs about.

clue.text: Stylish Kentish product? Worthless

parts.note: chic means stylish

indicators.note: a product is something made by working materials, so the county word is worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; Kentish means from Kent, an English county

explanation.surface: A fashionable product from the county of Kent turns out to be worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgar American slang for something petty, contemptible or of no value at all.

clue.text: Cyclops is right out of palm-grease and drink

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is put out, taken away from the word that follows

parts.note: the setter Cyclops speaking of himself: I am, shortened to I'm
greasing a palm is bribing someone

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being clear of corruption and of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is this puzzle's setter, so 'Cyclops is' stands for I'M. R for right is removed from BRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to take in liquid, especially alcohol, so the verb matches drinking.

clue.text: (see 28dn.)
(& 30ac.) "Yield to leader" blow

definitions.note: verb sense, slang for oral sex

parts.note: to give is to yield
a head is a leader; 'to' just joins the pieces

explanation.surface: An order to submit to the boss, then a blow is struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a punch; it is the vulgar verb for oral sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are coarse slang verbs for performing fellatio on someone.

clue.text: Take a piss, old man, before Kay's Ukrainian dance

indicators.note: placing one thing before another puts the earlier pieces first in the answer

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for urinating
your old man is your father, pa
Kay is how the letter K is said

explanation.surface: Someone relieves themselves and an old fellow goes ahead of Kay at a Ukrainian dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous Ukrainian folk dance with high leaps and squatting kicks by male dancers.

clue.text: (see 1ac.)
CIA hit abroad by exercises

indicators.note: abroad can mean scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreign assassination by the American spy agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese martial art is practised as a series of slow, flowing movements for health and balance.

clue.text: Bumper pee almost thwarted by device for shifting piss from the cellar

definitions.text: device for shifting piss from the cellar

indicators.note: thwarted plans are upset and disordered, so these letters are mixed up
almost means not quite the whole word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A huge urination is blocked by a gadget for pumping urine up from the basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss' is slang for beer, which a pub pumps up from its cellar to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's handpump draws ale from casks in the cellar, and piss is rude slang for weak beer.

clue.text: Novelist who's 80% defective?

indicators.note: eighty per cent keeps four parts in five, so the last fifth of the word is lost

parts.note: amiss means faulty or wrong

explanation.surface: A jibe that a certain writer is mostly faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley or Martin Amis, father and son English novelists.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley and Martin Amis were both celebrated English writers of fiction.

clue.text: Capital made when car hits bollocks, left having dropped off

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left falls away, so one letter is removed

parts.note: the Ford Ka is a small car
bollocks means nonsense, as does bull

explanation.surface: A car crash into someone's testicles, with the left one detached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hits' just places the car next to the nonsense word. One L of BULL drops off.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Afghanistan.

clue.text: Substantial work to do for Blair & Co!

parts.note: labour is hard, substantial work
a do is a party; 'to' just joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A big job lies ahead for Tony Blair and his colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair led Britain's Labour Party and was Prime Minister 1997-2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair and his associates formed the British political movement he led into government.

clue.text: (&22ac.) Poser who snorted: "Kelvin needs one to toss me off"

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters just before it are rearranged

parts.note: a means one
taken as written; 'to' just joins

explanation.surface: A model quoting someone called Kelvin's crude request.
explanation.walkthrough: A poser here is a model who poses; the supermodel was photographed apparently taking cocaine in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: The English supermodel was famously pictured snorting cocaine, a scandal splashed across the tabloids.

clue.text: (& 20ac.) Uplifting access to drink for the street lager lout?

definitions.text: Uplifting access to drink for the street lager lout?

parts.note: surface reading: drink as a mood-lifting escape
setter's reading: the tab lifted to open the can a drinker carries in the street

explanation.surface: Booze as a cheering route to oblivion for a lout drinking in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' sounds like cheering; it is literal, since the tab is lifted up to open a can.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal tab on a drinks can is lifted to open it, giving access to the beer inside.

clue.text: One only half wanking is easing up

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, so its first six letters are dropped

parts.note: wanking is crude slang for this

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly pleasuring himself is slowing down.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half of MASTURBATING is BATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Abating means lessening or subsiding, just as easing up means becoming less intense.

clue.text: Engaging in intercourse or "bollocking"

definitions.note: verb phrase, used with an object

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a severe telling-off, British slang

explanation.walkthrough: 'Intercourse' is used in its old sense of conversation. A bollocking is British slang for a severe reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking with someone is conversing; a scolding delivered face to face is also this phrase used as a noun.

clue.text: It helps protect my pole — rude, oo-er, etc, missus finally inside

indicators.note: inside places the selected letter within the reordered letters
rude means crude and unpolished, so the preceding letters are roughly reordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points at the very end of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of missus

explanation.surface: A smutty Carry On-style innuendo about protecting one's pole, oo-er missus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oo-er, missus' is the British comic catchphrase greeting a double entendre; here the pole is just a wooden post.
explanation.definitionFit: This tar-based oil is painted on fence posts and timber to preserve them against rot.

clue.text: Native American top grade soldier who's dropped, rejected, by House

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the preceding letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: A is the top grade
a paratrooper is dropped from a plane
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A top-grade soldier is thrown out of the army and turned away by a legislative House.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arapaho are an Indigenous people of the North American Great Plains.

clue.text: (see 15ac.)
Scruples? Question undergrad's first example of public relief

parts.note: Q is the abbreviation for question

indicators.note: first points at the opening letter of the student word

parts.note: the opening letter of undergrad
alms are charity given to the poor

explanation.surface: A student asks about a public lavatory, as 'public relief' suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public relief' sounds like urinating in a public toilet; it is poor relief, charity to the needy.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualms are pangs of conscience or doubts about whether something is right.

clue.text: (see 14ac.)
Steel's second promise …

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to give your word is to promise

explanation.surface: Someone called Steel makes a second pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Steel's is a link: Steel is the second promise; steel is poetic for a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is a literary word for a bladed weapon, as in cold steel.

clue.text: Donald's model parliament?

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's classic car
the Rump Parliament of 1648-53

explanation.surface: Asks whether Donald's ideal legislature is a model one.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'. The Rump Parliament was the purged English parliament after Pride's Purge.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump is the American businessman and president, so his surname fits his first name.

clue.text: Doubtful last 2/3 of an erection

indicators.note: keeping the last two thirds drops the opening third of the slang word

parts.note: a stiffy is slang for an erection

explanation.surface: A doubtful, only partly formed erection.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for uncertain or of questionable quality.

clue.text: … to get place finally in shameless junket

indicators.note: in places the chosen letter within the word that follows

parts.note: fast in its old sense of loose and immoral

indicators.note: finally points at the very last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of place

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone gets a seat at a brazen freebie.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on from 23 down only for the surface. Fast here means dissolute, as in a fast woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A junket is a lavish feast or celebration, often a jolly at someone else's expense.

clue.text: China boobs at the start, getting intimate

indicators.note: at the start places the breasts word ahead of the friend word

parts.note: a woman's bosom is her breasts
china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), hence pal

explanation.surface: Someone touches porcelain breasts and gets intimate.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate, as a noun, is a close friend or confidant.

clue.text: (+ 6dn.) Snap organ you're holding for the sailor-man

parts.note: to snap or pop is to make a sudden sharp sound
the organ is the eye, despite the suggestive surface

explanation.surface: Someone is told to snap the organ they are holding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ you're holding' points the mind rudely elsewhere; the organ is just the one you see with.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinach-eating cartoon character sings that he is the sailor man.

clue.text: Tabloid to sack slovenly female

parts.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper
a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper sacks an untidy woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives the word as informal for a slovenly, untidily dressed woman.

clue.text: (see 7ac.)
Women, in an offensively sexual way, paw — son approaches timidly

parts.words: Women, in an offensively sexual way
parts.note: crude slang for women viewed sexually
a paw is an animal's foot
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son awkwardly paws at women.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to act cautiously and avoid committing oneself, treading as softly as a cat.
